rationale: C03 plausibly supplied a material drafting template. Both memoranda begin by withholding approval of an individual relief bill that overrides a limitations bar, recount the claimant's administrative history, defend the generally applicable procedural system, and conclude that special relief would discriminate against numerous similarly situated persons. C18 reinforces the same orderly-procedure and discrimination language, while C13 is closely parallel in its defense of military correction boards against special legislative intervention, but neither matches the child's overall sequence as closely as C03.

shared_material.child_excerpt: This bill would confer jurisdiction on the Court of Claims, notwithstanding the applicable statute of limitations, to adjudicate the claim of Harry N. Duff
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The bill would permit the two named taxpayers to file claims for refund ... notwithstanding that the statute of limitations has barred the filing of such claims.
shared_material.explanation: Both introduce the bill as individualized relief that circumvents an otherwise controlling limitations period.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Traditionally, eligibility for retirement on account of physical disability has been determined by the military services in accordance with general provisions of law.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Congress has determined it to be sound policy to include in the revenue system a statute of limitations
shared_material.explanation: Each shifts from the beneficiary's facts to a defense of the established general legal and administrative framework.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Approval of this bill would discriminate against the many hundreds of individuals who have had their claims for disability retirement denied without benefit of judicial review.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This bill, by singling out two of these taxpayers for special relief from the statute of limitations, would unjustly discriminate against other taxpayers similarly situated.
shared_material.explanation: The concluding objection uses the same concrete rationale: exceptional relief for named beneficiaries would discriminate against a large class of similarly situated claimants.

shared_material.child_excerpt: It would also establish an undesirable precedent leading to other exceptions to the orderly procedure which is now provided for under general law
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The basic purposes underlying the statute of limitations continue in force even in cases where ... the interpretation of the law is changed
shared_material.explanation: Both reject case-specific exceptions because they would undermine the uniform operation and finality of general procedures.
